1: #!/usr/bin/env -S npx tsx
2: /**
3:  * Condition-aware piece evaluation. Value (an odds match) is one number; this tool asks the other
4:  * questions the owner raised: does a piece ever get paralysed? Does its contribution change with the
5:  * army's composition — guards, pawns, screens? Is a cheap piece balance-breaking in the right
6:  * condition? Does a dear piece go quiet in the wrong one?
7:  *
8:  *   tsx tools/conditions.ts --runs np-N,np-O,np-V-ortho,np-T
9:  *   tsx tools/conditions.ts --pair np-V-ortho,np-N          # paired by gameId (same openings)
10:  *
11:  * Per run it prints, for every piece type the run contains:
12:  *   presence   count/share of games where either army starts with the type
13:  *   owner armies  the count of separate armies that start with it
14:  *   moves per owner  the piece's moves per owner army
15:  *   still      share of owner armies where it made no move at all (paralysis)
16:  *   type present at end  share of owner armies with that type at the end; promotions can
17:  *                        replace original individuals, whose survival is not measured
18:  * and per run: decisive share, draws, capped, mean plies, White score.
19:  *
20:  * `--pair A,B` adds the paired difference over shared gameIds (same seed and ranks in the lab's
21:  * matched runs), plus the run's interaction counters so a condition can be read from the moves.
22:  */
23: import { createReadStream, existsSync } from 'node:fs';
24: import { createInterface } from 'node:readline';
25: import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
26: import { LETTERS } from '../src/rules/engine';
27: import type { GameRecord } from '../src/sim/game';
28: 
29: const flag = (name: string, dflt: string): string => {
30:   const i = process.argv.indexOf(`--${name}`);
31:   return i >= 0 && process.argv[i + 1] ? process.argv[i + 1] : dflt;
32: };
33: const RUNS = flag('runs', '').split(',').filter(Boolean);
34: const PAIR = flag('pair', '').split(',').filter(Boolean);
35: const pathOf = (id: string): string => (id.includes('/') ? id : `sim/out/${id}.jsonl`);
36: 
37: interface PieceStat {
38:   owners: number;
39:   present: number;
40:   moves: number;
41:   zero: number;
42:   survived: number;
43:   captures: number;
44: }
45: interface RunStat {
46:   id: string;
47:   games: number;
48:   decisive: number;
49:   draws: number;
50:   capped: number;
51:   plies: number;
52:   white: number;
53:   pieces: Map<string, PieceStat>;
54:   events: Record<string, number>;
55: }
56: const empty = (id: string): RunStat => ({ id, games: 0, decisive: 0, draws: 0, capped: 0, plies: 0, white: 0, pieces: new Map(), events: {} });
57: 
58: /**
59:  * One run, one piece type. A positive starting count of a valid single uppercase piece letter
60:  * (excluding K) on a side is ONE owner army for that type, no matter how many pieces of it the
61:  * side starts with — two Archers on one side are two pieces in one army, not two armies. `present`
62:  * is counted once per game: a type is present in a game if either side starts with it. `zero`
63:  * counts owner armies that made no move; `survived` counts owner armies with a positive end count;
64:  * `moves` and `captures` are summed over the armies. Activity and end-presence rates use owner
65:  * armies as their denominator; an empty run prints zero game rates and no piece rows.
66:  */
67: export async function scan(id: string): Promise<RunStat> {
68:   const file = pathOf(id);
69:   if (!existsSync(file)) throw new Error(`conditions: ${file} is missing`);
70:   const st = empty(id);
71:   const rl = createInterface({ input: createReadStream(file), crlfDelay: Infinity });
72:   for await (const line of rl) {
73:     if (!line) continue;
74:     const rec = JSON.parse(line) as GameRecord;
75:     st.games++;
76:     st.plies += rec.plies;
77:     st.white += rec.result;
78:     if (rec.result === 0.5) st.draws++;
79:     if (rec.reason === 'plyCap') st.capped++;
80:     if (rec.reason === 'checkmate' || rec.reason === 'adjudicatedResign') st.decisive++;
81:     for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(rec.events ?? {})) {
82:       const sum = Array.isArray(v) ? (Array.isArray(v[0]) ? (v as number[][]).flat().reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) : (v as number[]).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0)) : 0;
83:       st.events[k] = (st.events[k] ?? 0) + sum;
84:     }
85:     const seen = new Set<string>();
86:     for (const side of [0, 1] as const) {
87:       const pst = rec.stats[side];
88:       for (const [letter, count] of Object.entries(pst.start ?? {})) {
89:         if (!(count > 0) || !/^[A-Z]$/.test(letter) || !LETTERS.includes(letter) || letter === 'K') continue;
90:         const p = st.pieces.get(letter) ?? { owners: 0, present: 0, moves: 0, zero: 0, survived: 0, captures: 0 };
91:         p.owners += 1;
92:         if (!seen.has(letter)) { seen.add(letter); p.present += 1; }
93:         const moves = pst.moves[letter] ?? 0;
94:         p.moves += moves;
95:         if (moves === 0) p.zero += 1;
96:         if ((pst.survived[letter] ?? 0) > 0) p.survived += 1;
97:         p.captures += pst.captures[letter] ?? 0;
98:         st.pieces.set(letter, p);
99:       }
100:     }
101:   }
102:   return st;
103: }
104: 
105: const pct = (x: number): string => `${(100 * x).toFixed(1)}%`;
106: const show = (st: RunStat): void => {
107:   const g = st.games || 1;
108:   console.log(`\n${st.id}: ${st.games} games · decisive ${pct(st.decisive / g)} · draws ${pct(st.draws / g)} · capped ${pct(st.capped / g)} · plies ${(st.plies / g).toFixed(0)} · White ${(st.white / g).toFixed(3)}`);
109:   const letters = [...st.pieces.keys()].sort();
110:   console.log('  piece | presence | owner armies | moves per owner | still (no move) | TYPE PRESENT AT END | captures per owner');
111:   for (const l of letters) {
112:     const p = st.pieces.get(l)!;
113:     const owners = p.owners || 1;
114:     console.log(`    ${l.padEnd(5)} | ${`${p.present}/${st.games} (${pct(p.present / g)})`.padStart(14)} | ${String(p.owners).padStart(12)} | ${(p.moves / owners).toFixed(2).padStart(15)} | ${pct(p.zero / owners).padStart(15)} | ${pct(p.survived / owners).padStart(17)} | ${(p.captures / owners).toFixed(2)}`);
115:   }
116:   console.log('  Type present at end includes promotions; it does not track survival of original pieces.');
117:   const ev = Object.entries(st.events).filter(([, v]) => v > 0).map(([k, v]) => `${k} ${(v / g).toFixed(2)}`);
118:   if (ev.length) console.log(`  events/game: ${ev.join(', ')}`);
119: };
120: 
121: const main = async (): Promise<void> => {
122:   if (PAIR.length === 2) {
123:     const [a, b] = await Promise.all([scan(PAIR[0]), scan(PAIR[1])]);
124:     show(a); show(b);
125:     // Paired difference needs the records themselves, not the aggregates.
126:     const read = async (id: string): Promise<Map<number, GameRecord>> => {
127:       const m = new Map<number, GameRecord>();
128:       const rl = createInterface({ input: createReadStream(pathOf(id)), crlfDelay: Infinity });
129:       for await (const line of rl) { if (line) { const r = JSON.parse(line) as GameRecord; m.set(r.gameId, r); } }
130:       return m;
131:     };
132:     const [A, B] = await Promise.all([read(PAIR[0]), read(PAIR[1])]);
133:     const ids = [...A.keys()].filter(i => B.has(i));
134:     const mean = (xs: number[]): number => xs.reduce((x, y) => x + y, 0) / (xs.length || 1);
135:     const ci = (xs: number[]): number => {
136:       const n = xs.length; const m = mean(xs); if (n < 2) return NaN;
137:       const v = xs.reduce((x, y) => x + (y - m) ** 2, 0) / (n - 1);
138:       return 1.959964 * Math.sqrt(v / n);
139:     };
140:     const diff = (f: (r: GameRecord) => number): [number, number] => {
141:       const xs = ids.map(i => f(A.get(i)!) - f(B.get(i)!));
142:       return [mean(xs), ci(xs)];
143:     };
144:     const [res, resCI] = diff(r => r.result);
145:     const [dec, decCI] = diff(r => (r.result !== 0.5 ? 1 : 0));
146:     const [ply, plyCI] = diff(r => r.plies);
147:     console.log(`\npaired ${ids.length} games (${PAIR[0]} minus ${PAIR[1]})`);
148:     console.log(`  result ${res >= 0 ? '+' : ''}${res.toFixed(3)} ± ${resCI.toFixed(3)} · decisive ${dec >= 0 ? '+' : ''}${dec.toFixed(3)} ± ${decCI.toFixed(3)} · plies ${ply >= 0 ? '+' : ''}${ply.toFixed(1)} ± ${plyCI.toFixed(1)}`);
149:     return;
150:   }
151:   for (const id of RUNS) show(await scan(id));
152: };
153: 
154: if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? '').toString()) {
155:   if (!RUNS.length && PAIR.length !== 2) {
156:     console.error('usage: tsx tools/conditions.ts --runs a,b,c | --pair a,b');
157:     process.exit(2);
158:   }
159:   main().catch(e => { console.error(e); process.exit(2); });
160: }

1: /** Monte Carlo runner: a worker per core, one JSON line per game, resumable. */
2: import { closeSync, createWriteStream, existsSync, mkdirSync, openSync, readSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
3: import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
4: import { resolve as resolvePath } from 'node:path';
5: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
6: import { availableParallelism } from 'node:os';
7: import { Worker } from 'node:worker_threads';
8: import { GameRecord } from './game';
9: import { DEFAULT_RULES, Rules, ruleDiff, setRules } from '../rules/rules';
10: import { POOL } from '../rules/setup';
11: import { Job, OUT_DIR, RunSpec, buildJobs, loadSpec, parseFlags, paths, usePairs } from './spec';
12: import { sourceId, specKey } from './identity';
13: 
14: /**
15:  * Stamped on every game line: what a resume has to match. Readers ignore unknown fields.
16:  *
17:  * `rules` is the **full resolved rule set**, not a diff. A diff is read against the defaults of the
18:  * day, and those move, so a stored `rules: {}` does not mean today's game (LESSONS.md 2026-09-13):
19:  * sampling and replay have to set the exact rules a run played, and only the full set can do that.
20:  * `rulesKey` stays as the cheap comparison. `specKey` covers seed, pool, search/evaluation settings
21:  * and the eval-parameter files by content; `src` covers the engine code itself.
22:  */
23: export interface Stamp { rules: Rules; rulesKey: string; pool: string; specKey: string; src: string }
24: 
25: /**
26:  * The rules and pool a run plays under. `rulesKey` hashes the *whole* rule set, not the diff.
27:  * A new rule field re-keys *every* stored run and blocks its resume, so `kings` is left out of the
28:  * key for a run that plays none — the same "append, never move a historic key" discipline
29:  * `src/ai/zobrist.ts` follows. A run that does play a king hashes it, which is the whole point of
30:  * putting the choice in `Rules` (LESSONS.md 2026-09-14: a resumed control silently mixes pools).
31:  */
32: export function stampOf(spec: RunSpec): Stamp {
33:   const rules = { ...DEFAULT_RULES, ...spec.rules }; // exactly what run() puts in RULES
34:   const { kings, ...noKings } = rules;
35:   const keyed = kings[0] || kings[1] ? rules : noKings;
36:   return {
37:     rules,
38:     rulesKey: createHash('sha1').update(JSON.stringify(keyed)).digest('hex').slice(0, 8),
39:     pool: (Array.isArray(spec.backRanks) ? undefined : spec.backRanks?.pool) ?? POOL,
40:     specKey: specKey(spec),
41:     src: sourceId(),
42:   };
43: }
44: 
45: /** Line-per-line read of a possibly huge JSONL file. The last call has `complete = false` on a torn line. */
46: function eachLine(file: string, fn: (line: string, complete: boolean) => void): void {
47:   const fd = openSync(file, 'r');
48:   try {
49:     const buf = Buffer.alloc(1 << 22);
50:     let carry = '';
51:     for (;;) {
52:       const n = readSync(fd, buf, 0, buf.length, null);
53:       if (!n) break;
54:       // The files are our own JSON (ASCII, one line per game), so a chunk boundary cannot split a
55:       // character; it can only split a line, and `carry` holds that.
56:       const text = carry + buf.toString('utf8', 0, n);
57:       let start = 0;
58:       for (;;) {
59:         const nl = text.indexOf('\n', start);
60:         if (nl < 0) { carry = text.slice(start); break; }
61:         fn(text.slice(start, nl), true);
62:         start = nl + 1;
63:       }
64:     }
65:     if (carry) fn(carry, false);
66:   } finally { closeSync(fd); }
67: }
68: 
69: export interface RunScan {
70:   /** game id -> the arrangement it played. */
71:   configs: Map<number, string>;
72:   stamp: Stamp | null;
73:   games: number;
74:   /** Lines that are truncated (no newline) or not a game record. */
75:   bad: number;
76:   /** Stamped and unstamped records in one file, or two different stamps. */
77:   mixed: boolean;
78: }
79: 
80: /** What a file already holds. The stamp is the same on every line; a file written before it existed has none. */
81: export function readRun(file: string): RunScan {
82:   const configs = new Map<number, string>();
83:   const keys = new Set<string>();
84:   let stamp: Stamp | null = null, games = 0, bad = 0, stamped = 0;
85:   if (!existsSync(file)) return { configs, stamp, games, bad, mixed: false };
86:   eachLine(file, (line, complete) => {
87:     if (!complete) { bad++; return; }
88:     if (!line) return;
89:     let rec: GameRecord & Partial<Stamp>;
90:     try { rec = JSON.parse(line) as GameRecord & Partial<Stamp>; } catch { bad++; return; }
91:     if (typeof rec.gameId !== 'number' || typeof rec.configId !== 'string') { bad++; return; }
92:     games++;
93:     configs.set(rec.gameId, rec.configId);
94:     if (rec.rulesKey) {
95:       stamped++;
96:       const s: Stamp = {
97:         rules: (rec.rules ?? {}) as Rules, rulesKey: rec.rulesKey, pool: rec.pool ?? '',
98:         specKey: rec.specKey ?? '', src: rec.src ?? '',
99:       };
100:       if (!stamp) stamp = s;
101:       keys.add(s.specKey || s.rulesKey);
102:     }
103:   });
104:   return { configs, stamp, games, bad, mixed: (stamped > 0 && stamped < games) || keys.size > 1 };
105: }
106: 
107: /** Kept for callers that only want the map: the configs and the stamp of a stored run. */
108: export function doneGames(file: string): { configs: Map<number, string>; stamp: Stamp | null } {
109:   const { configs, stamp } = readRun(file);
110:   return { configs, stamp };
111: }
112: 
113: /**
114:  * A run resumes from its JSONL by game id, so the stored games have to be the ones this spec plays
115:  * now. After a change to `POOL`, `DEFAULT_RULES`, the seed, the evaluation files or the source they
116:  * are not, and the file then holds two experiments that every reader adds up as one: `pb-ab-base`
117:  * was 1 544 games under the two-guard pool plus 56 under the one-guard pool, and the A/B it
118:  * controlled was void (LESSONS.md 2026-09-14). Throws rather than appending; returns the games to
119:  * skip. A file with no stamp at all is read-only history: give the run a new id instead of
120:  * resuming a game whose rules are unknown.
121:  */
122: export function checkResume(spec: RunSpec, jobs: Job[], file: string): Map<number, string> {
123:   const { configs, stamp, games, bad, mixed } = readRun(file);
124:   if (!games && !bad) return configs;
125:   const newId = 'Give the run a new id';
126:   if (bad) {
127:     throw new Error(`[${spec.id}] refusing to resume ${file}: ${bad} line(s) are torn or unreadable (a partial write). ${newId}, or repair the file from a backup.`);
128:   }
129:   if (mixed) {
130:     throw new Error(`[${spec.id}] refusing to resume ${file}: its ${games} games carry more than one stamp or a mix of stamped and unstamped records. ${newId}.`);
131:   }
132:   const distinct = (xs: Iterable<string>): number => new Set(xs).size;
133:   const badCfg = [...configs].find(([id, cfg]) => jobs[id]?.configId !== cfg);
134:   if (badCfg) {
135:     throw new Error(`[${spec.id}] refusing to resume ${file}: its ${configs.size} stored games played ${distinct(configs.values())} arrangements, this spec plays ${distinct(jobs.map(j => j.configId))} over ${jobs.length} games (game ${badCfg[0]} is "${badCfg[1]}" in the file, "${jobs[badCfg[0]]?.configId ?? 'not played'}" now). ${newId}, or list \`backRanks\` in the spec to replay the stored ones.`);
136:   }
137:   if (!stamp) {
138:     throw new Error(`[${spec.id}] refusing to resume ${file}: its ${games} stored games carry no rule/source stamp (written before stamping existed), so the rules they played are unknown. ${newId}.`);
139:   }
140:   const now = stampOf(spec);
141:   if (stamp.rulesKey !== now.rulesKey || stamp.pool !== now.pool) {
142:     throw new Error(`[${spec.id}] refusing to resume ${file}: its ${games} stored games played rules ${JSON.stringify(ruleDiff(stamp.rules))} (key ${stamp.rulesKey}) on pool ${stamp.pool}, this spec plays ${JSON.stringify(ruleDiff(now.rules))} (key ${now.rulesKey}) on pool ${now.pool}. ${newId}.`);
143:   }
144:   if (stamp.specKey !== now.specKey) {
145:     throw new Error(`[${spec.id}] refusing to resume ${file}: the seed, arrangements, search settings or evaluation inputs changed (stamp ${stamp.specKey}, this spec ${now.specKey}). ${newId}.`);
146:   }
147:   if (stamp.src !== now.src) {
148:     throw new Error(`[${spec.id}] refusing to resume ${file}: its ${games} games were played by source ${stamp.src}, this source is ${now.src}. ${newId}.`);
149:   }
150:   return configs;
151: }
152: 
153: const hms = (s: number): string =>
154:   s < 0 || !isFinite(s) ? '?' : `${Math.floor(s / 3600)}h${String(Math.floor(s / 60) % 60).padStart(2, '0')}m${String(Math.floor(s) % 60).padStart(2, '0')}s`;
155: 
156: export async function run(spec: RunSpec, nWorkers: number): Promise<void> {
157:   mkdirSync(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true });
158:   // The sampler reads the rules too (`bishopsOppositeColours` rejects a draw), and it runs here in
159:   // the main thread, not in a worker. Without this the one rule that only constrains *which back
160:   // ranks exist* would be invisible to its own run.
161:   setRules(spec.rules);
162:   const { jsonl, summary } = paths(spec.id);
163:   const all = buildJobs(spec);
164:   const done = checkResume(spec, all, jsonl);
165:   const jobs: Job[] = all.filter(j => !done.has(j.gameId));
166: 
167:   console.log(`[${spec.id}] ${spec.games} games (${done.size} already done), ${jobs.length} to play on ${nWorkers} workers -> ${jsonl}`);
168:   console.log(`[${spec.id}] depth ${spec.ai.depth ?? '-'}, ${spec.openingRandomPlies ?? 0} random opening plies, ply cap ${spec.maxPlies}, pairs ${usePairs(spec) ? 'on' : 'off (both sides identical; --pairs forces them on)'}`);
169:   // Printed because a dropped `--rule` or `--values` is otherwise invisible until the report is wrong.
170:   console.log(`[${spec.id}] rules ${JSON.stringify(ruleDiff(spec.rules ?? {}))}, values ${JSON.stringify(spec.values ?? {})}`);
171:   if (!jobs.length) { writeSummary(spec, jsonl, summary, 0); return; }
172: 
173:   const out = createWriteStream(jsonl, { flags: 'a' });
174:   const stamp = stampOf(spec); // after the record, so `gameId` stays the first key on the line
175:   const t0 = Date.now();
176:   let next = 0, finished = 0;
177: 
178:   const tick = setInterval(() => {
179:     const s = (Date.now() - t0) / 1000;
180:     const rate = finished / s;
181:     const line = `[${spec.id}] ${finished}/${jobs.length}  ${rate.toFixed(1)} games/s  ETA ${hms((jobs.length - finished) / rate)}`;
182:     process.stdout.write(process.stdout.isTTY ? `\r${line}   ` : `${line}\n`);
183:   }, 2000);
184: 
185:   await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
186:     const workers = Array.from({ length: Math.max(1, Math.min(nWorkers, jobs.length)) }, () => {
187:       const w = new Worker(new URL('./worker.ts', import.meta.url), { workerData: spec });
188:       w.on('message', (rec: GameRecord) => {
189:         out.write(JSON.stringify({ ...rec, ...stamp }) + '\n');
190:         finished++;
191:         if (next < jobs.length) w.postMessage(jobs[next++]);
192:         else { w.terminate(); if (finished === jobs.length) resolve(); }
193:       });
194:       w.on('error', reject);
195:       return w;
196:     });
197:     for (const w of workers) if (next < jobs.length) w.postMessage(jobs[next++]);
198:   });
199: 
200:   clearInterval(tick);
201:   await new Promise<void>(res => out.end(res)); // flush before writeSummary reads the file back
202:   const secs = (Date.now() - t0) / 1000;
203:   process.stdout.write(`${process.stdout.isTTY ? '\r' : ''}[${spec.id}] ${finished} games in ${hms(secs)} (${(finished / secs).toFixed(1)} games/s)\n`);
204:   writeSummary(spec, jsonl, summary, secs);
205: }
206: 
207: /**
208:  * Streamed, not `readFileSync`: the file is now on the order of a gigabyte and reading it as one
209:  * string throws `ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG` (>512 MB) — which is exactly how the inherited Q6 chain
210:  * ended with `exit 1` and a summary that still reported its 686-game prefix (BASELINE.md).
211:  */
212: function writeSummary(spec: RunSpec, jsonl: string, summary: string, secs: number): void {
213:   const reasons: Record<string, number> = {};
214:   let n = 0, score = 0, wins = 0, draws = 0, plies = 0;
215:   eachLine(jsonl, (line, complete) => {
216:     if (!complete || !line) return;
217:     let r: GameRecord;
218:     try { r = JSON.parse(line) as GameRecord; } catch { return; }
219:     n++;
220:     reasons[r.reason] = (reasons[r.reason] ?? 0) + 1;
221:     score += r.result; plies += r.plies;
222:     if (r.result === 1) wins++; else if (r.result === 0.5) draws++;
223:   });
224:   const d = n || 1;
225:   writeFileSync(summary, JSON.stringify({
226:     spec, games: n, seconds: +secs.toFixed(1),
227:     whiteScore: +(score / d).toFixed(4),
228:     whiteWins: wins, draws, blackWins: n - wins - draws,
229:     meanPlies: +(plies / d).toFixed(1), reasons,
230:   }, null, 2) + '\n');
231:   console.log(`[${spec.id}] summary -> ${summary}`);
232: }
233: 
234: if (process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === resolvePath(process.argv[1])) {
235:   const spec = loadSpec(process.argv.slice(2));
236:   const f = parseFlags(process.argv.slice(2));
237:   const workers = typeof f.workers === 'string' ? +f.workers : availableParallelism();
238:   const fail = (e: unknown): void => { console.error(e); process.exitCode = 1; };
239:   // Not `await`: a top-level await would make this an async module, which breaks any CJS importer.
240:   // The experiments are imported lazily for the same reason, and to keep the import graph acyclic.
241:   if (typeof f.experiment === 'string') {
242:     import('./experiments').then(m => m.runExperiment(f.experiment as string, spec, workers, f)).catch(fail);
243:   } else {
244:     run(spec, workers).catch(fail);
245:   }
246: }

20: function filesUnder(dir: string): string[] {
21:   const st = statSync(dir);
22:   if (!st.isDirectory()) {
23:     return dir.endsWith('.ts') ? [dir] : [];
24:   }
25:   const out: string[] = [];
26:   for (const name of readdirSync(dir).sort()) {
27:     const p = join(dir, name);
28:     const s = statSync(p);
29:     if (s.isDirectory()) out.push(...filesUnder(p));
30:     else if (p.endsWith('.ts')) out.push(p);
31:   }
32:   return out;
33: }

35: export function sourceId(root = '.'): string {
36:   const h = createHash('sha1');
37:   const base = normalize(root);
38:   for (const dir of SRC_ROOTS) {
39:     const target = join(base, dir);
40:     const files = filesUnder(target);
41:     for (const f of files) {
42:       const rel = relative(base, f);
43:       h.update(rel);
44:       h.update('\0');
45:       h.update(readFileSync(f));
46:       h.update('\0');
47:     }
48:   }
49:   return h.digest('hex').slice(0, 12);
50: }

194:     let gap: number | undefined;

196:     if (moves.length < openingPlies) {

224:       ...(nodes === undefined ? {} : { nodes }),
